processing: Raw pu-erh pressed into round cakes at the state factory in Menghai, in the same family as Red Mark. The details of its recipe are not well recorded.
harvest_season: Not recorded. Spring leaf is generally the most prized in pu-erh.
appearance_dry: Aged dark brown cakes in a Zhongcha wrapper with a green character for tea at the centre.
appearance_liquor: Deep amber to chestnut, as is usual for raw pu-erh of this age.
appearance_wet: Dark brown, softened leaf, typical of raw pu-erh of this age.
taste_profile: Few dependable tasting notes exist. Raw pu-erh of this age typically gives wood and earth with a gentle sweetness.

brewing.notes: General advice for old raw pu-erh, with a brief rinse and short early steeps.

vintage_note: Originals are sold by version and rough date, with the big-character Green Mark placed from the 1950s to the mid-1960s. These are auction pieces. The same name on modern cakes tells you little, so check the year and factory.
description:
Green Mark is Red Mark's sibling, a raw pu-erh round cake named for the green character for tea on its wrapper. It came from the same early factory work at Fohai, today's Menghai.

Collectors usually rank it below Red Mark. An auction account quotes the later factory head Tang Qingyang as saying Green Mark used leaf from around Menghai and Red Mark the best leaf from Mengla, which would be a difference in raw material as well as colour, though it is a single account.

Its cup is thinly recorded, so go by what raw pu-erh of this age generally does: wood, earth and a gentle sweetness, with short steeps and hot water.

Versions matter here. Ask whether a cake is the big-character type and what evidence supports its date, because the wrapper alone proves little.
history:
Green Mark traces back to Fan Hejun's experimental factory in Fohai, where he was sent in 1939; about a year later, trial Red Mark and Green Mark cakes were produced. The China Tea Company's Eight Zhong trademark followed in 1951.

Auction accounts place big-character Green Mark production from the 1950s to the mid-1960s. Those dates are the market's working chronology, and factory records for it are not widely available.
